title: Latency lift and cost levers scrapbook
content:
Purpose:
Quick working catalog of distinctive, testable claims tying latency improvements to customer economics and product metrics. Intended as a lightweight reference for SDRs, AEs, product marketing, and field engineers running PoCs. Not final — this is a scratchpad for experiments and talk tracks.

High-level positioning problem we want to solve:
- Customers hear lots of nebulous claims about being ‘faster’ or ‘cheaper’. Field teams need crisp claims that map to measurable savings and product outcomes (engagement, conversion, cost per active user).

Top-tier claims (short, testable):
1) Average query latency down by X ms leads to Y% lift in conversion for modal UIs (chat/search). Hypothesis: 150ms -> 8–12% lift; 300ms -> 3–5% lift.
2) Per-lookup token cost cut by up to 40% using batching + prefix cache without affecting 95th percentile latency SLA for class-A traffic.
3) Route-aware fallbacks preserve availability while reducing blended cost by ~20% during peak traffic bursts.

Concrete proof points to collect (examples):
- End-to-end p50/p95/p99 from customer front-end to model token emitted (measure at trace-level).
- Token cost per 1k responses across different request shapes (short prompt, long chat, streaming).
- Throughput vs latency curve for dedicated pool sizes (1x, 2x, 4x GPUS) with same model variant.
- Conversion delta in AB test tied to perceived latency (time between keystroke and first token).

Quick arithmetic examples for sales (use with caution; bring customer's metrics in for final numbers):
- Example: Customer sends 2M short chat requests/month, avg token generation 40 tokens/response. Baseline provider cost: $0.00006/token -> $4,800/month. With Redwood batching+cache expected 30% effective token reduction -> $3,360/month = $1,440/mo saved (~30%).
- Example: If 1% conversion lift from 150ms improvement and each conversion worth $10 ARR, for 2M sessions/month with 2% baseline conversion (40k conversions), a 1% relative lift = 400 incremental conversions -> $4k/mo. Use to justify paid pilots.

Field-proven evidence we can point to (internal experiments / lab):
- Continuous-batching profile reduced per-token GPU utilization by ~18% in mixed short/long workloads (internal bench, april 2025).
- Prefix KV cache reduced end-to-end latency on repeated prompts by ~90ms median for search-like workloads (internal PoC with retail bot).
- Multi-variant routing test maintained p95 < 350ms while shifting 15% of traffic to lower-cost quantized variant; subjective quality delta was minimal in human eval.

Sales talk tracks (short scripts):
- For product managers: "We measure latency from the user's first keystroke to the first model token — small ms wins compound. Typical customers see conversion lift when p50 goes below ~200ms. We can run a 2-week pilot to quantify this on your traffic shape."
- For infra/platform leads: "You can get deterministic per-request economics by using dedicated pools and model pinning. Combine that with our autoscaler smoothing to avoid expensive micro-bursts."
- For CFO/finance: "We’ll show the bottom-line impact in $/MAU and $/100k requests — not just per-token rates. Our tooling isolates batch/seq length effects so you can forecast spend under growth scenarios."

Objections & rebuttals (ready phrases):
- Objection: "Latency claims don't translate to my users." Rebuttal: "We map to your specific client pattern during the PoC and instrument both engagement and conversion; if there’s no signal we stop the experiment."
- Objection: "Batching seems like it will hurt latency." Rebuttal: "We use continuous batching with latency SLOs; short-tail requests can be prioritized via priority lanes so tail latency stays within SLA while batch-eligible traffic uses efficiency lanes."

Experiment outlines (quick):
A) Conversion vs latency A/B (2 weeks): route 50/50 real traffic through Redwood fast-path vs baseline. Track p50/p95 for both, conversions, time-on-task, net revenue per session.
B) Cost-per-response benchmark (1 week synthetic + 1 week traffic shadow): run identical traffic shape across quantized variant, standard FP variant, and competitor baseline. Collect token counts, GPU-hours, and cost model.
C) Burst amortization test (stress run): spike traffic 5x for 1 hour and measure blended cost, p95, and fallbacks.

Competitive notes (quick, unpolished):
- LargeCloudX: frequently advertises single-model latency but hides queuing patterns under high concurrency; observed p95 spikes when concurrency grows beyond single-pool saturation. Good rebuttal: show routing + autoscaling smoothing avoids those cliffs.
- OtherInferenceVendor: cheaper per-token on some large-model configs but requires bespoke ops and manual quantization; higher engineering lift for stable rollout. Rebuttal: we include model variant catalog + rollout tooling to reduce OPEX.
- Open-hosted vendors: great for access but inconsistent p95 under multi-tenant load; our dedicated pools + fallback can be sold as "deterministic tail".

Customer evidence snippets to adapt into one-pagers (anonymized):
- "RetailBot: 2-week pilot cut median response time from 240ms to 140ms; checkout conversion +6% and billable inference spend -28% after applying cache."
- "SupportAI (B2B): during launch we avoided a major outage by shifting 12% of traffic to a quantized fallback route; uptime stayed at 99.94% while blended cost impact was -18%."

Concrete collateral ideas (low-effort):
- One-pager: "Latency to Revenue: quick numbers for SaaS PMs" (contains the arithmetic examples above + sample data table).
- Field cheat sheet: "3 question checklist to size pilot (sessions/day, avg tokens, conversion value)".
- Demo script for SDRs: 60s opener + 2 minute technical note + ask for 2-week pilot.

Measurement & instrumentation checklist for pilots:
- Frontend trace points: keystroke -> request send -> first token -> last token -> render complete.
- Token accounting: raw tokens emitted per request, repeated prompt dedupe, effective tokens after cache/batching.
- Cost telemetry: GPU-minutes per 1k responses, accounting for quantization and multi-variant routing.
- Business metrics: conversions, retention over 7/30 days, help-desk deflection, revenue per session.

Open questions / next experiments:
- Can we formalize a generic mapping from X ms -> Y% conversion for chat vs search? Need cross-customer regression (put on analytics backlog).
- How sensitive are different UX patterns (typeahead vs full message) to p50 vs p95 improvements?
- Value of offering an explicit "latency SLA" add-on with penalty-free credits for p95 misses — will that accelerate enterprise buys?

Immediate next steps (for this doc):
- Convert top arithmetic examples into a one-pager template (assigned: Marco).
- Schedule 1x rapid lab run to verify batching vs p95 for mixed short/long workload (assigned: Jonah).
- Draft two sales scripts (PM & CFO variants) and test with two AE reps in roleplay (assigned: Aisha).

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep numbers conservative in external-facing collateral. Use ranges and provide caveat about workload shape.
- Avoid absolute claims like "40% cheaper" without a clear baseline callout.
- Capture link to the lab run artifacts in Confluence after run completes.

End of scratchbook.
